# Updates on Tariffs, Liquidity, and Strategy

Report 168 | Published 2025-08-03 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2025-8-3/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/168.json)

Tariff pressure and Strategy’s preferred-share financing.

The TGA undershoot forecast was wrong. The preferred-share analysis correctly distinguishes maturity risk from dividend deferral, but overstates par stability and eventual recovery. STRC grew substantially while its yield rose rather than converging toward seven percent; STRF and STRC delivered very different returns.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Claims

### 168-C01

**Tariffs impose material domestic costs.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | tariff-incidence |
| Source blocks | 11, 12, 13 |
| Thesis family | tariff-incidence |

The static goods-import arithmetic is internally consistent and subsequent research found nearly 90% of tariff incidence fell on US firms and consumers. This does not imply that unchanged import-price indexes prove zero foreign burden in every sector or that static revenue would be collected.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

Domestic firms and consumers bore nearly 90% of the burden.

### 168-C13

**Premium equity issuance can increase Bitcoin per share.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | bitcoin-treasury-nav-accretion |
| Source blocks | 69, 85 |
| Thesis family | bitcoin-treasury-nav-accretion |

Issuing shares above net asset value and buying the same underlying asset can increase assets per share after costs. Enterprise-value-to-gross-Bitcoin mNAV is not identical to common-equity-to-net-assets NAV and must be adjusted for senior claims. Share-count dilution and per-share accretion can occur together.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Issue price above existing net assets per share
- Net proceeds invested without offsetting losses
- Senior claims and transaction costs included

New net assets per share exceed old net assets per share when proceeds per new share exceed the prior net asset value per share.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

## Analytical tools and charts

- **Treasury cash target:** Use daily quarter-end balances, not weekly averages Visual inspection: not performed.
- **Strategy capital stack:** Separate maturity, seniority, cumulative claims and legal availability Visual inspection: not performed.
- **mNAV issuance bands:** Policy guidance can change; gross and net NAV differ Visual inspection: not performed.
- **Bitcoin stress scenarios:** Asset coverage is not recurring cash-flow coverage Visual inspection: not performed.

## Framework lessons

- A security can avoid legal default and still impose a large investor loss.
- Price stabilization intent is not guaranteed par redemption.

## Verification limitations

- Current page snapshot is not an authenticated publication-date version.
- A missing horizon is not replaced with an invented author deadline.
- Market sensitivities use vendor adjusted closes and do not reconstruct portfolio execution.
